title: One letter along: how much work?
hook: A window moves one letter. Do you have to add up all its letters again?

knows: what a hash is: a number made from some data (hash-bucket-pileup)
doesNotKnow: that the hash of a sliding window can be updated instead of recomputed
that equal hashes still need a letter-by-letter check

misconception: Comparing a pattern against every window of a text means re-reading every letter of every window.
objective: The learner can explain that sliding a window one letter updates a sum hash with one subtraction and one addition, so a slide costs the same however long the pattern is, and that a window with an equal sum is only a flag that must be checked.

claims.text: With A = 1 ... F = 6, the 9 windows of 5 letters in FEBCDAFFABCDE have sums 20, 15, 16, 20, 18, 16, 18, 16, 15; the pattern ABCDE has sum 15, so windows 2 (EBCDA, a false flag) and 9 (ABCDE, a match) are flagged.
claims.source: Builder's node run of sum(window) over EBCDAFFABCDE, window 5, A = 1: sums 15 16 20 18 16 18 16 15; pattern 15; flags at 0-based starts 0 and 7 (the stage counts windows from 1). | v3 2026-10-14 (demo-builder): text changed from EBCDAFFABCDE to FEBCDAFFABCDE so the learner slides before meeting the false flag. Builder's node run: sums 20 15 16 20 18 16 18 16 15. Reopened.

claims.text: Each slide is one subtraction and one addition: 20 - 6 + 1 = 15, then 15 - 5 + 6 = 16, and so on.
claims.source: Node: sums[i+1] = sums[i] - value(text[i]) + value(text[i+5]) for all 7 slides reproduces the 8 window sums. | v3 2026-10-14 (demo-builder): first slide is now FEBCD -> EBCDA (20 - 6 + 1 = 15). Reopened.

claims.text: Sliding across all 9 windows reads 21 letters (5 for the first window, then 2 per slide for 8 slides); adding each window up again reads 45 (9 windows x 5 letters).
claims.source: 5 + 7 x 2 = 19 and 8 x 5 = 40 (node). The counter on the stage uses the same formulas after each slide. 'Letters read' here counts letters added to or removed from a sum; letters compared in a check are not counted. | v3 2026-10-14 (demo-builder): 5 + 8 x 2 = 21 and 9 x 5 = 45 for the new 13-letter text; the reveal computes both from the learner's slide count. Counter hidden until lock-in. Reopened.

claims.text: EBCDA has the same sum as ABCDE (15) but is a different string: checking letters finds E is not A at the first letter. The sum hash cannot tell one order of letters from another.
claims.source: Sum ignores order: any rearrangement of ABCDE sums to 15 (node: EBCDA = 5+2+3+4+1 = 15). The check compares left to right and stops at the first mismatch, letter 1.

claims.text: Only the two end letters change, so a wider window would still cost 2 per slide: an updatable hash makes each slide cost the same, however long the pattern is.
claims.source: Each slide touches two letters whatever the window width k, against k letters to re-add. Rabin-Karp: Karp and Rabin 1987, 'Efficient randomized pattern-matching algorithms', IBM J. Res. Dev.; CLRS 32.2 (to be checked by the fact-checker; the stage uses a plain sum, not their polynomial hash). | v3 2026-10-14 (demo-builder): reworded to point at the stage's '−' and '+' chips and the 'kept' bracket. Reopened.

claims.text: Each slide used two letters, the one leaving (marked −) and the one arriving (marked +); the 4 letters marked 'kept' were already in the sum.
claims.source: Window i (letters i..i+4) and window i-1 (letters i-1..i+3) share the 4 letters at positions i..i+3; the stage draws a 'kept: already in the sum' bracket under them on every slide (Demo.tsx). Added v3 2026-10-14 by demo-builder.

recall.question: A window of 1,000 letters slides one place along a text. To update its sum hash you...
options: subtract the letter that left and add the one that arrived
recall.why: One letter leaves and one arrives, so two operations update the sum however wide the window is.
